questions.question: Which state is famous for celebrating the Majuli festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Majuli is a river island located in the Brahmaputra River in Assam, which is the world's largest river island and the cultural capital of the state.
 
• **The Majuli festival is a popular cultural festival celebrated in Assam to showcase the state's rich cultural heritage and traditional art forms.**
 
• **It is a three-day festival held in November every year.**
 
• The festival includes various cultural activities such as dance performances, folk music, traditional sports, and handicraft exhibitions.
 
• **The festival also promotes environmental awareness and sustainable development practices.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Famous festivals of **Manipur** include** Gang-Ngai, Lui-Ngai-Ni, Yaosang, Cheiraoba, Kang and Heikru.** 
 
• Famous festivals of **Sikkim** include **Maghe Sankranti, Sonam Lochar, Losar, Holi, Ramnawami (Chaite Dasain) and Good Friday. **
 
• **Famous festivals of Meghalaya include the ****Garo**** Wangala festival, Shad Suk, Mynsiem, and Nongkrem Dance.**

questions.question: In India, which organization maintains the national highways?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**National Highways Authority of India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of national highways in India.**
 
• NHAI is an autonomous agency under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and was established in 1988.
 
• NHAI is responsible for the construction of new national highways, the widening of existing highways, and the maintenance of highways across the country.
 
• NHAI also collects tolls on the national highways to generate revenue for their maintenance and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Border Road Organisation (BRO) is responsible for the construction and maintenance of roads in border areas and is a part of the Indian Army.
 
• **State governments and their respective Public Works Department are responsible for the development and maintenance of state highways and other roads within their respective states.**
 
• The** Indian road network** is the second-largest in the world, with a total length of **5.5 million kilometers.**
 
• The national highways in India account for only 2% of the total road network but carry 40% of the total road traffic.

questions.question: Select the correct statement.

options.text: Mitochondria and nucleus are found in bacteria.
Ribosomes, mitochondria and lysosomes are found in animal cells.
Chloroplast, ribosomes and nucleus are present in fungal cell.
Mitochondria and nucleus is absent in plant cell.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes, mitochondria and lysosomes are found in animal cells.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes **are found in all cells, including animal cells.

 
 
• **Ribosomes are responsible for synthesizing proteins.**
 
 
 
• Mitochondria are the energy-producing organelles in animal cells.
 
 
• Mitochondria are organelles that are found in eukaryotic cells (cells that have a nucleus) and are responsible for producing energy in the form of ATP.
 
 
 
• Lysosomes are also found in animal cells and are responsible for breaking down waste materials.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bacteria do not have a nucleus and their energy-producing organelles are called "plasmids," not mitochondria.
 
• **In fact, plant cells have additional organelles such as chloroplasts, cell walls, and** large central vacuoles** that are not found in animal cells.**
 
• Chloroplasts are organelles that are found in plant cells and are responsible for photosynthesis, the process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.
 
• **Fungal cells are eukaryotic cells that have a nucleus and organelles such as ribosomes and a nucleus.**
 
• They do not have chloroplasts, which are only found in plant cells.

questions.question: Which of the following expressions is correct regarding the gross fiscal deficit?

options.text: Gross fiscal deficit = Net borrowing at home − Borrowing from RBI + Borrowing from abroad
Gross fiscal deficit = Net borrowing at home + Borrowing from RBI + Borrowing from abroad
Gross fiscal deficit = Net borrowing at home + Borrowing from RBI − Borrowing from abroad
Gross fiscal deficit = Net borrowing at home − Borrowing from RBI − Borrowing from abroad

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross fiscal deficit = Net borrowing at home + Borrowing from RBI + Borrowing from abroad.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross fiscal deficit refers to the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue.**
 
• **It takes into account all types of borrowing, including borrowing from RBI and borrowing from abroad.**
 
• Typically, a significant increase in capital expenditures or an income shortfall causes a fiscal deficit.
 
• To construct long-term assets like factories, buildings, and other developments, capital expenditures are needed.
 
• Typically, a deficit is funded by borrowing from the nation's central bank or by raising funds on the capital markets through the issuance of bonds and treasury bills, among other instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Net borrowing at home refers to the difference between the government's borrowing from the market and its repayment of past loans.**
 
• **Borrowing from RBI** refers to the government's borrowing from the central bank.
 
• **Borrowing from abroad** refers to the government's borrowing from foreign sources.

questions.question: Who was the last king of the Shunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Devabhuti.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The last king of the Shunga dynasty was Devabhuti.**
 
• **Shunga dynasty ruled over a major part of northern India from the 2ⁿd century BCE to the 1st century BCE.**
 
• The Shunga dynasty was preceded by the Maurya dynasty and succeeded by the Kanva dynasty.
 
• The Shunga period saw the revival of Hinduism and Sanskrit literature, after the decline of Buddhism under the Mauryas.
 
• Devabhuti was a weak and ineffective ruler, who was overthrown by his minister Vasudeva Kanva, leading to the end of the Shunga dynasty.
 
• The Kanva dynasty ruled for a brief period of about 45 years, before being replaced by the Satavahanas in the Deccan region.
 
• **The Satavahanas were contemporaries of the later Shunga kings, and their most famous ruler was Gautamiputra Satakarni, who defeated the Shunga ruler Vasumitra.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pushyamitra Shunga was the founder of the Shunga dynasty.**

 
 
• **He ruled from 185 BCE to 149 BCE.**
 
 
 
• **Bhavabhuti was a renowned Sanskrit playwright and poet who lived in the 8th century CE, several centuries after the end of Shunga dynasty.**
 
 
• His plays are regarded as being on par with Kalidasa's.
 
 
 
• Shashanka was a king of Gauda region in present-day West Bengal during the 7th century CE, again several centuries after the end of Shunga dynasty.
 
 
• **The Bengali calendar is attributed to Shashanka.**

questions.question: Who received the Nobel Prize 'for his research in the stereochemistry of organic molecules and reactions' in 1975?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vladimir Prelog.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The person who received the Nobel Prize 'for his research in the stereochemistry of organic molecules and reactions' in 1975 is Vladimir Prelog.**
 
• Prelog was a Croatian-Swiss chemist who made significant contributions to the field of stereochemistry, which is the study of the spatial arrangement of atoms in molecules.
 
• His research focused on the three-dimensional structure of molecules and their interactions with other molecules, which helped to explain how chemical reactions occur.
 
• **Prelog's work also led to the development of new drugs and materials with specific properties.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lipscomb** received the prize in **1976** for his work on the structure of **molecules.**

 
 
• **He was an American inorganic and organic scientist who studied biochemistry, boron chemistry, theoretical chemistry, and nuclear magnetic resonance.**
 
 
 
• Wilkinson received the Nobel Prize in 1973 for his discoveries in organometallic chemistry.
 
 
• Wilkinson was a chemist who established homogeneous transition metal catalysis and inorganic chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Flory** received Nobel Prize in **1974** for his contributions to **polymer chemistry.**

questions.question: Which Social Media Platform's plea against summons to the Delhi Assembly was rejected by the Supreme Court in July 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Facebook.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **In July 2021, the Supreme Court of India rejected Facebook's plea against the summons issued by the Delhi Assembly's Peace and Harmony Committee.**
 
• The summons were related to allegations of the social media platform's inaction against hate speech and posts promoting violence during the Delhi riots in February 2020.
 
• The committee had sought Facebook's representatives to appear before it for questioning, but the company argued that the summons was unconstitutional and violated its privacy rights.
 
• However, the Supreme Court ruled that the Delhi Assembly had the power to summon individuals and entities for its proceedings, and Facebook could not claim absolute immunity from such summons.
 
• **The court also directed Facebook to cooperate with the committee's investigation and provide relevant documents and information.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Twitter has also faced similar issues with the Delhi Assembly and the Indian government over its handling of content related to farmers' protests and other sensitive topics.**
 
• The American multimedia instant messaging software and service Snapchat was created by Snap Inc., formerly known as Snapchat Inc.
 
• Instagram is a social networking website that allows users to share photos and videos.
 
 
• **It is owned by Meta Platforms.**

questions.question: Lake Victoria is in which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tanzania, Uganda, and Kenya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lake Victoria** **is in** **Uganda, Tanzania, and Kenya.**
 
• **The lake is the largest in Africa and the second-largest freshwater lake in the world.**
 
• It is an important source of water for the surrounding countries and supports a** large fishing industry.**
 
• The lake is also a popular tourist destination, known for its beautiful scenery and diverse wildlife.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Three nations share the lake's landmass: **Tanzania (49%), Uganda (45%), and Kenya (6%).**
 
• **The first British person to map the lake was John Hanning Speke, an explorer who went on an expedition with Richard Francis Burton in 1858 and dubbed it after Queen Victoria.**
 
• Numerous native fish species have become extinct as a result of invasive fish like the Nile perch.
 
• A species of jumping spider (family Salticidae) unique to the area surrounding Lake Victoria in Kenya and Uganda is called Evarcha culicivora.
 
• **It mostly consumes female mosquitoes for food.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62d1583dfd7ddf58c44089991fdfece31ce1fe15c6198791bd5774ccdb3392a0.png]

questions.question: Which hill is a part of the Meghalaya plateau?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaintia Hills.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jaintia Hills is a part of the Meghalaya plateau, which is located in the northeastern part of India.**
 
• The Meghalaya Plateau is a part of the larger Deccan Plateau and consists of several hills and valleys.
 
• The Jaintia Hills are known for their rich biodiversity, including several endemic species of flora and fauna.
 
• **The hills are also home to several indigenous tribes, including the Jaintia and Pnar communities.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cardamom Hills:-**

 
 
• Located in the **Western Ghats of southern India**, the Cardamom Hills are known for their **cardamom spice**, which is grown in the cool elevations of the hills.
 
 
 
• **The Nilgiri Hills are located in the Western Ghats.**
 
 
• **Nilgiris is renowned for producing bauxite in addition to tea and eucalyptus oil.**
 
 
 
• **Anaimalai Hills are also known as the Elephant Hills.**
 
 
• These are located in Tamil Nadu and Kerala and are known for their rich wildlife and scenic beauty.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://th.bing.com/th/id/R.95b47e72a099ecfcd3c6e93bf1089525?rik=3lxoLxDFPbN3wg&riu=http%3a%2f%2fmapsof.net%2fuploads%2fstatic-maps%2findia_physical.png&ehk=m04e9H09UnhSeu0OmFpTB2M7v8oXqGJrmvasRiRcc9I%3d&risl=&pid=ImgRaw&r=0]

questions.question: Prajjwala Challenge, a nationwide initiative to provide a platform to thoughtful minds to bring about change was launched by

options.text: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Rural Development.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prajwala Challenge** is a nationwide initiative launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development.**
 
• The Prajwala Challenge was launched in **2019 **and is open to** individuals, startups, and organizations** to submit innovative ideas and solutions for rural development.
 
• The objective of the Prajwala Challenge is to** identify and support innovative **solutions that can be scaled up and replicated to address the challenges faced by **rural communities** in areas such as agriculture, water, sanitation, health, education, and livelihoods.
 
• The Prajwala Challenge offers **funding, mentorship, and networking **opportunities to the selected participants to help them implement their ideas and solutions.
 
• The Ministry of Rural Development has also launched other initiatives such as the** Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana **(DDU-GKY) and the **National Rural Livelihoods Mission** (NRLM) to promote** rural development and livelihoods.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On **September 25, 2014,** Union Ministers** Nitin Gadkari and Venkaiah Naidu** introduced DDU-GKY in honor of** Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya's** 98th birthday.

 
 
• "Transform rural poor youth into an **economically independent** and globally relevant workforce" is the mission statement of DDU-GKY.
 
• Youth in the **15–35 age **range are the target demographic. 
 
 
 
• The goal of the** National Rural Livelihood Mission **(NRLM) initiative is to organize **rural impoverished people **and encourage** self-employment.**
 
 
• **​**The purpose of this initiative is to **enable self-employment** by grouping the impoverished into** Self Help Groups (SHGs). **​

questions.question: Ishwari Prasad is associated with which of the following Indian classical dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ishwari Prasad **is associated with the Indian classical dance form of **Kathak.**
 
• **The roots of the Kathak Lucknow Gharana may be traced back to Sri Ishwari Prasadji, an Allahabad inhabitant of the Handia Tehsil.**
 
• Kathak is a North Indian classical dance form that originated in the Mughal era and is known for its intricate footwork and graceful movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri** is a classical dance form from **Manipur** in Northeast India.

 
 
• It is characterized by its **slow and graceful movements.**
 
 
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama form from **Kerala **in South India.
 
 
• It is known for its elaborate makeup and costumes, and its use of facial expressions and hand gestures to convey emotions.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam **is a classical dance form from** Tamil Nadu** in South India.
 
 
• It is known for its complex rhythms and expressive gestures.

questions.question: Who founded Lucknow Gharana of Kathak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwari Prasad.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• Ishwari Prasad was a prominent dancer and musician who developed the Lucknow gharana of Kathak. 
 
• He was born in Lucknow in 1856 and learned Kathak from his father, Thakur Prasad. 
 
• He blended the traditional Kathak style with elements of Persian and Urdu culture to create the Lucknow gharana. 
 
• **Some of the distinctive features of this gharana include the use of chakkars (spins), thumris (classical songs), and abhinaya (expressive storytelling).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sitara Devi was a famous Kathak dancer.
 
 
• Devi met Rabindranath Tagore when she was quite young.
 
• Out of fondness, he called her the "empress of dance," or Nritya Samragni.
 
 
 
• **Birju Maharaj is a renowned Kathak dancer and choreographer.**
 
 
• **India's second-highest civilian award, the Padma Vibhushan, was given to Birju Maharaj in 1986.**
 
 
 
• Rukmini Devi was a famous Bharatanatyam dancer and founder of Kalakshetra Foundation.
 
 
• She was the first female nominee for the Rajya Sabha in Indian history.

questions.question: Which of the following cities was sacked by victorious armies after the battle of Talikota?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayanagar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The battle of Talikota was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccan Sultanates in 1565.**
 
• The victorious armies of the Deccan Sultanates, comprising **Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Bidar,** and **Golconda,** sacked the city of **Vijayanagar **after winning the battle.
 
• Vijayanagar was the capital city of the Vijayanagara Empire, situated in present-day Hampi, Karnataka.
 
• The city was known for its grandeur and opulence, with magnificent temples, palaces, and markets.
 
• The defeat and sacking of Vijayanagar marked the decline of the Vijayanagara Empire and the rise of the Deccan Sultanates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ahmadnagar was a city in Maharashtra.**

 
 
• It was ruled by the Nizam Shahi dynasty during the 16th century.
 
 
 
• Bijapur was one of the Deccan Sultanates that participated in the battle of Talikota and sacked Vijayanagar after the victory.
 
 
• The city of Bijapur is renowned for its historically significant and architecturally significant monuments that were constructed under the Adil Shahi reign.
 
 
 
• **Golconda was another Deccan Sultanate that was part of the victorious army in the battle of Talikota and contributed to the sacking of Vijayanagar.**
 
 
• **It was known for its diamond mines and was later annexed by the Mughal Empire.**

questions.question: Which five-year plan aimed to increase the rapid growth in food grains production?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Seventh Five-Year Plan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The seventh Five-Year Plan was implemented from 1985 to 1990.**
 
• The main objective of this plan was to achieve rapid growth in food grain production and increase self-sufficiency in food.
 
• The plan aimed to increase the food grains production from 155 million tonnes in 1984-85 to 200 million tonnes by the end of the plan period.
 
• **The Seventh Five-Year Plan also focused on increasing employment opportunities, improving infrastructure, and promoting social justice.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The sixth Five Year Plan was implemented from 1980 to 1985.**

 
 
• It focused on poverty alleviation and rural development.
 
 
 
• **The Fifth Five-Year Plan was implemented from 1974 to 1979.**
 
 
• It aimed to achieve self-reliance in agriculture and industry.
 
 
 
• **The Eighth Five-Year Plan was implemented from 1992 to 1997.**
 
 
• It focused on human development, employment generation, and infrastructure development.

questions.question: In which month of 2021 was the All India Survey on Migrant Workers under the overall guidance of an Expert Group came into effect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The All India Survey on Migrant Workers was conducted under the overall guidance of an Expert Group constituted by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.**
 
• It came into effect in **April.**
 
• The survey aimed to collect data on the socio-economic profile of migrant workers, their skill sets, employment status, and their access to social security benefits.
 
• The survey was conducted in 4,200 sample villages/wards and covered 1.14 lakh migrant workers across all states and union territories of India.
 
• The survey was conducted through a combination of telephonic interviews and face-to-face interviews, following all COVID-19 safety protocols. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In August 2020, the Ministry of Labour and Employment announced that it would conduct a survey on migrant workers to assess their employment status and skill sets. **
 
• In June 2021, the Supreme Court directed the Centre and state governments to conduct a fresh survey to identify and provide relief to migrant workers stranded during the second wave of COVID-19. 
 
• In February 2021, the Ministry of Labour and Employment had launched a portal for migrant workers to register themselves and avail welfare schemes.

questions.question: As per the 2011 Census, what is the density of the population of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**382 persons/km2.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **As per the 2011 Census, the density of the population of India is 382 persons/km².**
 
• This means that on average, there are 382 people living in every square kilometer of India's land area.
 
• **India is the second most populous country in the world after China, and its population density is much higher than the global average of 56 persons/km².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Population density is a measure of the number of people living in a given area.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the total population of an area by its land area.
 
• India's population density has been steadily increasing over the years, and it is projected to reach 464 persons/km² by 2021.
 
• The high population density in India has led to a number of challenges such as overcrowding, urbanization, and environmental degradation.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to qualify for Covenanted service?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyendra Nath Tagore.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyendra Nath Tagore was the first Indian to qualify for Covenanted service.**
 
• **He cleared the Indian Civil Service (ICS) examination in 1863 and joined the Bengal Presidency Civil Service.**
 
• **He was a member of Bramho Samaj. **
 
• Tagore was a prominent member of the Tagore family and was the elder brother of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore.

questions.question: The first Women's Cricket World Cup was hosted by which of the following countries?

__

• The tournament was played in a round-robin format with four teams - **England, Australia, New Zealand, and Jamaica.**
 
• England emerged as the champions by winning all three of their matches, while Australia finished as runners-up with two wins.
 
• The Women's Cricket World Cup is held once every four years and the current champions are England, who won the 2017 edition held in England and Wales.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It featured a total of 7 teams, including two unique teams – Young England and International XI, which usually do not feature in regular World Cups. 
 
• Each match was of 60 overs, which was different from today's 50-over format.
 
• This tournament proved to be a milestone for women's cricket – it showed that women can also compete at the international level.

questions.question: Plant varieties like bamboo, epiphytes, aini, semul, gutel and mundane are found in which type of Indian forest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moist tropical forest.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The plant varieties mentioned in the question, such as bamboo, epiphytes, aini, semul, gutel, and mundane are found in moist tropical forests in India.**
 
• **Moist tropical forests are characterized by high rainfall and high humidity, with temperatures ranging from 20-28oC.**
 
• These forests are also known as evergreen forests because the trees here do not shed their leaves all at once, unlike deciduous forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bamboo is a fast-growing plant that is widely used in construction, paper-making, and as a source of food for animals.
 
• Epiphytes are plants that grow on other plants, such as trees but do not harm them.
 
 
• They obtain their nutrients from the air and rain.
 
 
 
• Aini, semul, gutel, and mundane are all tree species found in moist tropical forests in India.
 
 
• **Aini is also known as Indian gooseberry and is used in Ayurvedic medicine.**
 
• **Semul, also known as silk cotton tree, is used to make pillows and mattresses.**
 
• **Gutel is a type of hardwood tree, and mundane is a type of fig tree.**
 
 
 
• Alpine forests are found at high altitudes, typically above 3,500 meters, and are characterized by low temperatures and short growing seasons.
 
• **Montane temperate forests are found in areas with cooler temperatures and higher elevations than tropical forests but lower than alpine forests.**
 
• Dry tropical forests are found in regions with less rainfall and are characterized by a different set of plant species compared to moist tropical forests.

questions.question: Dry ice, ammonium chloride, naphthalene balls, and camphor, all these compounds are an example of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sublimable substances.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sublimation is the process in which a solid substance directly converts into its gaseous form without going through the liquid phase.**
 
• **Dry ice, ammonium chloride, naphthalene balls, and camphor exhibit sublimation on heating. **
 
• Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, which sublimates at -78.5 degrees Celsius and is commonly used as a cooling agent because it undergoes sublimation, transitioning directly from solid to gas without becoming liquid. This property makes it useful for keeping things cold without leaving behind liquid residue. So while it's not a traditional "cooling agent " like ice packs, it functions effectively in cooling applications due to its sublimation process.
 
• Ammonium chloride, naphthalene balls, and camphor are also sublimable substances that are used for various purposes such as in moth repellents, decongestants, and medicinal ointments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cooling agents are substances that are used to lower the temperature of a system, and all the given compounds can act as cooling agents due to their sublimation properties.**
 
• Inflammable substances are those that can easily catch fire and burn, while solidifying agents are substances that can convert liquids into solids.
 
• None of the given compounds fall under these categories.
 
• Dry ice is commonly used in the transportation of perishable goods as it can maintain a low temperature for an extended period.
 
• Ammonium chloride is used as a flux in the soldering of metals and in the production of dry batteries.
 
• **Naphthalene balls are used as a moth repellent and to prevent musty odors in closets and storage spaces.**
 
• Camphor is used in medicinal ointments and as a flavoring agent in food and beverages.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India came into existence on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26 January 1950.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **26 January 1950 date marks the inauguration of the Supreme Court of India.**
 
• It replaced the Federal Court of India and was established under the Constitution of India.
 
• The Supreme Court is the highest judicial body in the country, and its decisions are binding on all other courts in India.
 
• **The first Chief Justice of India was Hiralal J. Kania, who served from 1950 to 1951.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Chief Justice of India and up to 33 other judges make up the Supreme Court, which has broad authority in the form of original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.
 
• According to Article 142 of the Constitution, the court has the inherent authority to issue any order that is thought to be required for the sake of full justice, and the President is obligated to carry it out.
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India was founded on 1 April 1935 to respond to economic troubles after the First World War.**
 
• **15 August 1947 is the date when India gained independence from British rule.**
 
• **2 October 1952 is the date when the first postage stamp was issued in India.**

questions.question: Khan Bahadur led the revolt of 1857 from:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Khan Bahadur led the revolt of 1857 from Bareilly.**
 
• **Bareilly was an important centre of the revolt of 1857 and was the site of several battles between the rebels and the British.**
 
• **In 1857, during the Indian uprising against British colonial control, Khan Bahadur established his own government at Bareilly as a show of protest.**
 
• During the Rebellion of 1857, the British took Bareilly prisoner.
 
• At seventy, Khan Bahadur rose up in rebellion against the British.
 
• He took a number of actions to guarantee unity between Muslims and Hindus.
 
• He battled the colonial government in order to free the Motherland.
 
• **In Bareilly, the capital of Rohilkhand, Khan Bahadur Khan Rohilla proclaimed the state's independence on May 31, 1857.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi was the site of the first major uprising of the revolt of 1857 and was the centre of power for the rebels during the early stages of the rebellion.**
 
• Kanpur was another important centre of the revolt of 1857 and was the site of the infamous massacre of British women and children by the rebels under the leadership of Nana Sahib.
 
• Lucknow was the site of a prolonged siege by the rebels and was the site of several battles between the rebels and the British.
 
• The siege of Lucknow was one of the most significant events of the revolt of 1857.

questions.question: Which was the first country to incorporate Fundamental Duties in its Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**USSR.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **USSR (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) was the first country to incorporate Fundamental Duties in its Constitution in 1936.**
 
• **The concept of Fundamental Duties was introduced in the Indian Constitution in 1976 through the 42nd Amendment, but India was not the first country to incorporate it in its Constitution.**
 
• Fundamental Duties were recommended by the Swaran Singh Committee in 1976, and their importance became apparent during the internal emergency of 1975–1977.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **moral duties** that all Indian citizens have to support the **country's unity **and foster a **sense of patriotism** are known as the **Fundamental Duties.**
 
• **Both people and the country are subject to the obligations outlined in Part IV–A of the Constitution.**
 
• Similar to the Directive Principles, they cannot be enforced in court unless legislative legislation specifically provides for their enforcement.
 
• Albania is known for its isolationist policies and had a communist government until the 1990s. 
 
• Poland is a country in Europe that had a socialist government until the 1980s.
